newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk military says Islamist PM signs warning text.
newsitem.headline: Turk military says Islamist PM signs warning text.

text.p: Turkey's military-dominated National Security Council (NSC) said on Wednesday Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan had signed a council statement demanding a crackdown on religious activism.

"(The NSC statement) was signed by Prime Minister Erbakan without any changes," NSC secretary general Ilhan Kilic was quoted as saying by state-run Anatolian news agency on leaving the prime ministry.
The powerful council demanded in a weekend statement that Erbakan's coalition crack down on religious activism, which the NSC said was largely fostered by his Islam-based Welfare Party.
Erbakan had initially refused, arguing that democracy meant his government answered only to parliament and not the army, in comments which exacerbated the dispute.
"The signature, the crisis...these problems have been completely overcome," Kilic told reporters after half-an-hour of talks with Erbakan.

The apparent deadlock with the army, which has ousted three civilian governments in 37 years, had put strains on Erbakan's coalition with Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's conservative True Path Party and sent shares tumbling 15 percent in Istanbul this week.

Deputy Prime Minister Ciller had suggested the crisis could also damage the country's chances of joining the European Union. Leading EU figures spoke out earlier this week against Turkey's membership.
Ministers from the eight-month-old coalition were to meet on Thursday for a cabinet meeting.
